title: How Alex Slater scaled Quitter to $500K/month: first-mover ads, influencer CPMs, copying winners
summary: Alex Slater (20) explains how his anti-gooning app Quitter grew to 1.5M downloads and about $500K/month, and how App Mafia's course made $480K in three days. Useful on first-mover advantage, view-guaranteed influencer deals, reverse-engineering winners and volume. Much of the episode is lifestyle chat.

principles.text: Being first in a niche means no competition, easy conversion, and pricing power, plus cheap early ads.
principles.quote: We had the first mover advantage and so getting people in the door was really easy and getting people to pay for it was really easy because there's no competition. We can charge whatever we want.

principles.text: Reverse-engineer a proven app's monetization, paywall and influencer playbook, then replicate it in your niche.
principles.quote: I broke down exactly how they make money, exactly how they do the pay wall, exactly how they work with influencers, replicated it, and it worked.

principles.text: Pay influencers per view (CPM guarantees) so spend stays tied to results and you're almost always profitable.
principles.quote: we do view guarantees. So I think we pay around $2 uh CPM.

principles.text: Check an influencer's audience demographics before signing them, not just their view counts.
principles.quote: We got to look at the demographics always. That's like one of the prerequisites to like signing influencer.

principles.text: Volume is the lever: do more output per day and keep taking shots to make micro adjustments.
principles.quote: the most important part is volume. Double like double volume. Try to figure out to do two days of re two days worth of revenue one day.

principles.text: Knowing when you're wrong and killing an idea is a core founder skill, especially if it lacks marketing leverage.
principles.quote: one of the skills in being an entrepreneur is like knowing when you're wrong and knowing when to like bite the bullet sometimes and like call it quits.
